title: ApproxGNN: A Pretrained GNN for Parameter Prediction in Design Space Exploration for Approximate Computing
problem: Design space exploration for approximate accelerators requires expensive evaluation of QoR-cost tradeoffs for many parameter configurations.
motivation: Efficient parameter prediction accelerates design space exploration and enables rapid prototyping of approximate accelerators.
method: The approach uses a Graph Neural Network—an AI model that understands how things connect together—to predict two outcomes: how good the computed results will be and how much computing power they'll need. Rather than training a fresh model for each new design problem, the team trains one model on multiple approximate computing scenarios and reuses that knowledge to predict performance on new problems (a technique called transfer learning). This saves time because the pre-trained model already understands the general patterns of how design choices affect quality and cost.
key_novelty: This is the first work to use a pre-trained Graph Neural Network that can transfer its knowledge across different approximate computing design problems, eliminating the need to build and train a new model from scratch for each scenario.
contributions: GNN model for QoR/cost prediction in approximate computing
limitations: Transfer learning scope and generalization to novel approximate computing paradigms not detailed.
